item.title: How a noncitizen suspected killer got caught and released by Newsom-appointed judge: Timeline
item.description: Surveillance video allegedly shows Marcos Iriarte-Valdez in a tactical vest stabbing retiree Todd Stewart in a quiet East Bay suburb of California.
item.content:encoded:
The suspect charged in the stabbing death of a California man in an otherwise quiet East Bay suburb has a history of prior arrests and originally entered the U.S. during the George W. Bush administration, according to records.

Marcos Iriarte-Valdez, alternatively identified by DHS as Marcos Valdezusper, was arrested Friday at his home in Contra Costa County, California, after police said he stabbed and killed 68-year-old retiree Todd Stewart during an apparent burglary attempt.

"The investigation is ongoing and our understanding of the incident may change as more individuals are interviewed and evidence is collected and analyzed," a statement from the Martinez Police Department read in-part.

Iriarte-Valdez was "legally admitted" to the U.S. in 2007, according to information provided by ICE. Fox News Digital reached out to the agency for further clarity on what happened between then and when he was deemed an "illegal alien" by DHS on X more recently.

DEADLY HOSPITAL STABBING PUTS NEWSOM UNDER PRESSURE OVER ICE DETAINER FIGHT

Iriarte-Valdez hails from Venezuela but has Spanish citizenship.

Iriarte-Valdez was arrested earlier this year on at least two charges of residential burglary with persons present stemming from incidents in Orinda on April 29, according to Martinez police.

He was out on pretrial release for those charges when he was arrested again on Aug. 4 for violating his home-detention monitoring rules, according to authorities.

FEDS ADMIT FAILURE TO DISCLOSE MURDER WARRANT TO JUDGE WHO ORDERED RELEASE OF DOMINICAN MIGRANT

One day later, Contra Costa Superior Court Judge Nichelle Holmes, an appointee of Gov. Gavin Newsom, released Iriarte-Valdez on his own recognizance and returned him to home-detention monitoring.

Then, on Aug. 6, surveillance video showed Iriarte-Valdez wearing a tactical vest and emerging from a Cadillac before he was seen stabbing Stewart, who could be heard screaming in pain.

That video helped police obtain a warrant from Contra Costa Superior Court for Iriarte-Valdez on charges of murder and committing a felony while on own-recognizance release, according to court records.

Just after 6PM PT Friday, a Contra Costa SWAT team arrested Iriarte-Valdez at his home. His bail was initially set at $1.1 million.

ICE LODGES DETAINER FOR ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT ACCUSED OF TRYING TO DISARM VIRGINIA POLICE OFFICER

Contra Costa County Democratic District Attorney Diane Becton filed a felony complaint against Iriarte-Valdez that included one count of murder with several "special circumstances" cited under California law that could result in stiffer penalties.

The complaint includes a special-circumstance allegation of murder during a burglary, which could lead to life imprisonment without parole if Iriarte-Valdez is convicted, as well as "enhancement" allegations involving the use of a knife and committing an offense while out on conditional release.

"Our office will pursue this case with diligence and integrity to hold Iriarte-Valdez fully accountable under the law for this devastating act of violence," Becton said in a statement.

"Our thoughts are with the victim’s loved ones and the larger community as they navigate this unimaginable loss."

MAN CHARGED IN CRASH THAT KILLED MOTHER AND TWO YOUNG SONS HAS ICE DETAINER, PRIOR DWI CONVICTIONS

Becton’s office said Iriarte-Valdez pleaded not guilty Wednesday during a hearing in which Judge David Goldstein called him a "risk to public safety" and ordered him held without bail. Former Democratic Gov. Jerry Brown appointed Goldstein.

Another Newsom appointee, Judge Michael Nieto, is set to preside over Iriarte-Valdez’ case during a preliminary hearing in nearby Richmond on Sept. 1.

According to court documents, Iriarte-Valdez is set to appear separately before Holmes on Sept. 9 on his original burglary charges from April.

ICE placed a federal detainer on Iriarte-Valdez on Saturday and said he has also been charged with crimes including inflicting corporal injury on a spouse, receiving stolen property, trespassing, loitering and entering a noncommercial dwelling.

TOM HOMAN WARNS ICE SURGE COMING TO NEW YORK CITY AS MAMDANI BOASTS ABOUT SANCTUARY STATUS

DHS did not immediately explain what happened between 2007 and 2026 that could have led to Iriarte-Valdez being considered an "illegal alien" now. Common scenarios include a noncitizen overstaying a temporary visa, violating visa terms, becoming a lawful permanent resident and later having that status revoked because of a criminal conviction, or abandoning permanent resident status through extended residency abroad.

White House border czar Thomas Homan described the incident as a tragic case of "politics of a sanctuary jurisdiction."

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

"There's nothing against the sanctuary law in California for a deputy to pick a phone up and say ‘hey this guy's being let go in an hour’," Homan told "Fox & Friends." "This person is dead because Governor Newsom and the State of California put politics -- hatred of President Trump -- over public safety."

Fox News Digital reached out to Holmes, Becton and Newsom for further comment.

item.title: Haley Stevens condemns Hasan Piker but rallies behind El-Sayed after narrow primary loss
item.description: Haley Stevens says Hasan Piker "should be condemned" while pledging support for Abdul El-Sayed ahead of the Michigan Senate race against Mike Rogers.
item.content:encoded:
Rep. Haley Stevens, D-Mich., said Wednesday that far-left streamer Hasan Piker "should be condemned," publicly breaking with a prominent campaign ally of Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed as Democrats try to unite after a bruising Michigan primary and hold an open battleground Senate seat in November.

Stevens, who lost the Democratic Senate primary to El-Sayed last week, reiterated her criticism of Piker on NewsNation's "Vargas Reports" when host Elizabeth Vargas asked about the streamer’s involvement in the race.

"I believe he should be condemned. I do. I said that, that's what I was just saying to you," Stevens said. "I was saying, On election day, I said that, and if asked again, and you're asking me, I do think he should be condemned. I don't know what the guy has to do with Michigan."

DAVID MARCUS: WHY IT'S TOO LATE FOR DEMS TO DITCH PIKER AND HIS AMERICA-HATING SOCIALISM

Republican National Committee national spokesperson Natalie Baldassarre, responding to the growing scrutiny of Piker, told Fox News Digital on Wednesday that Democrats should formally disavow him.

"Hasan Piker is a Hamas-hugging radical with a long history of threatening rape and violence against those he disagrees with," Baldassarre said. "Democrats would do right to disavow him, but they'll continue to bend to his will like spineless, useful idiots."

Stevens also rejected the idea that Piker represented the Democratic Party and questioned his place in its politics.

"I don't agree with Piker. I don't think he's a part of the Democratic Party, she said. "You know, maybe Bernie can talk to him. I don't really know."

MICHIGAN DEMOCRAT HALEY STEVENS BACKS EL-SAYED AFTER NARROW PRIMARY DEFEAT, CALLS SOCIALISM ‘DANGEROUS’

Piker became one of El-Sayed's most visible outside supporters during the Michigan primary, appearing alongside the candidate at campaign events and joining him at a Detroit pool party on the eve of the election. The appearance came as El-Sayed's association with Piker became an increasingly prominent issue in the closing stretch of the race.

Hours before polls closed, Stevens told Fox News Digital that El-Sayed should distance himself from the streamer and denounce his rhetoric.

"I don't believe Mr. Piker lives here in our state. I do think his rhetoric should be denounced," Stevens said. "I do think that my opponent should distance himself from him."

ABDUL EL-SAYED SAYS RALLYING WITH HASAN PIKER DOESN'T MEAN HE ENDORSES 'AMERICA DESERVED 9/11' REMARK

Despite that criticism, Stevens said after losing the primary that she would support El-Sayed against Republican nominee Mike Rogers in November. During a Tuesday appearance on Fox News’ "America’s Newsroom," Stevens said Democratic primary voters had made their choice while emphasizing that she would not abandon her own political positions.

"I believe in democracy. He won the majority of the votes, and I'm going to continue to stand by my positions," Stevens said.

El-Sayed previously rejected some of Piker's most controversial remarks while resisting pressure to sever ties with him. When NBC host Kristen Welker asked El-Sayed about Piker's past statement that "America deserved 9/11," El-Sayed called the remark a "dumb statement" and said the United States did not deserve the terrorist attacks while criticizing what he characterized as "cancel culture."

"Of course it was a dumb statement and, of course, I think Hasan himself would say that was a dumb statement," El-Sayed said.

El-Sayed will face Republican Mike Rogers in November for an open seat created by the retirement of Sen. Gary Peters, D-Mich., one of the contests expected to help determine control of the Senate.

Fox News Digital reached out to Piker, El-Sayed, Sanders and Stevens for comment, but did not immediately receive a response.

item.title: White House launches interactive map tracking billions in suspected fraud
item.description: The White House launched The Fraud Ledger, an interactive dashboard tracking $230 billion in suspected fraud uncovered by JD Vance's task force.
item.content:encoded:
The White House on Thursday launched a public tracking dashboard documenting billions of dollars in alleged waste, fraud and financial corruption uncovered by the Trump administration across federal programs.

The interactive website, The Fraud Ledger, highlights data collected since January 2025 by the White House Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a panel chaired by Vice President JD Vance.

The platform details ongoing investigations, criminal charges, financial recoveries and enforcement actions undertaken by the task force since its establishment earlier this year.

VICE PRESIDENT VANCE SAYS MIGRANT COMMUNITIES SHOW 'CLEAR PATTERN' IN FEDERAL FRAUD AS INVESTIGATIONS WIDEN

Data compiled from public records and federal agency submissions reveals significant figures in uncovered fraud.

The Small Business Administration led all agencies with $122.9 billion in uncovered fraud, followed closely by the Department of Health and Human Services with $96.2 billion, according to the White House tracker.

Overall, the White House reports that the task force has uncovered roughly $230 billion in suspected fraud.

Furthermore, the administration claims to have halted $56 billion in fraudulent payments intended for criminal actors, while executing more than $55 billion in total enforcement actions.

DOJ CHARGES 10 SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA DEFENDANTS IN LARGEST FEDERAL HEALTHCARE FRAUD CRACKDOWN IN US HISTORY

The interactive portal features a national map detailing the task force’s top 10 highest-impact enforcement actions since January 2025.

Among its key highlights, the site documents the suspension of federal payments to the Los Angeles Homeless Services Authority pending the outcome of a fraud investigation, while also featuring a section displaying individuals arrested on charges in the most egregious cases.

Additionally, the site highlights dozens of ongoing prosecutions tied to Medicare and Medicaid fraud, the alleged misuse of COVID-19 relief loans and the massive Feeding Our Future fraud case in Minnesota.

Combating federal fraud has remained a central priority for the Trump administration through coordinated investigations and law enforcement crackdowns, including a major Justice Department operation in June that charged more than 450 individuals for their alleged involvement in schemes totaling over $6.5 billion.

item.title: Little League World Series coach divides fans with his 'Jesus' message during mound visit
item.description: An ESPN hot mic captured Drew Breivogel's viral mound visit sermon during a Little League World Series regional game, dividing fans online.
item.content:encoded:
An Arizona baseball coach sent the internet into a tizzy this week when he gave his pitcher a sermon on the mound during a Little League World Series regional game.

Drew Breivogel went viral Wednesday night when an ESPN hot mic caught his faith-filled message to his pitcher in the fourth inning. With the game hanging in the balance and two runners on, Breivogel called time, walked to the mound and gave his player some simple advice to help calm the nerves.

"I'm so proud of you," he said. "I've known you since you were eight. Remember Zacchaeus in the Bible? Someone planted that tree, 30, 40 years prior, so he could climb up into it. Salvation. We're talking salvation. It's a baseball game, right?

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

"If you walk the next five guys Jesus is still Lord. If you strike out the next five guys, guess what? Jesus is still Lord. I love you. Have some fun."

Nothing like a little church on a Wednesday night! Brings me back to my childhood.

Social media, shockingly, was all over the place on this video. Some loved the message. Others were confused by it, given it didn't include any real strategy on how to work out of the jam.

Nothing about mechanics, or 'buckling down,' or throwing strikes, or hitting spots.

A quick check of the box score says that Hawaii would score four runs in the inning en route to a 5-2 win to stave off elimination. Not great.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

"How about a scouting report?" one fan commented on the now-viral video. "Some advice about mechanics? Something that may actually help the kid learn baseball? If I was the pitcher I would of pushed my coach away."

"If I’m struggling on the mound on national tv and my coach comes up to me and starts this BS instead of advice or mechanical changes, I’m quitting," added another.

Said a third: "Then the next 3 hitters reached base safely because there was no gameplan instilled during the mound visit. This was a coach using TV to make himself look good he knew he was Mic’d up, that was his BIG moment."

All fair points. But it's also Little League. A big spot? Absolutely. But these are 12-year-old kids. How much of a scouting report do they really have on them? Little League baseball is the Wild Wild West. I grew up in. I've seen it all. I've heard it all. Admittedly, I was never part of a mound meeting quite like that.

So, again, I see both sides here. That little sermon did remind me of a great quote my old Little League coach used to tell us when we were nervous before a game:

"If you strike out, there are a billion people in China who won't care tomorrow."

Makes sense. Made us feel a little better.

But, we also never got close to reaching Williamsport or the Little League World Series.

So perhaps we could've used a different approach.

item.title: Mystery surrounds Little League coach's ejection during championship game after ESPN cuts his mic
item.description: Team Kentucky assistant coach Matthew Teague was ejected by the home plate umpire during the Great Lakes Little League regional finals game.
item.content:encoded:
Was this a quick trigger or was the Little League umpire well within his rights to kick this coach out of the game?

During Wednesday's Great Lakes regional finals game, with a trip to the Little League World Series on the line, Team Kentucky assistant coach Matthew Teague was ejected by the home plate umpire.

Down 6-0 in the top of the 4th and running out of time for a comeback, Teague was seen meeting with one of his hitters and turning his attention to the umpire who had just called out a Kentucky hitter on a tough strike three call for the second out.

IDAHO TEEN UMPIRE DELIVERS ULTIMATE REALITY CHECK TO COACH COMPLAINING ABOUT WALK-UP MUSIC

"Oh boy, Matthew Teague has (been) ejected from the game," the ESPN announcer said while adding that the umpire warned Teague not to come closer to the batter's box.

Were there words exchanged between Teague and the umpire? If so, ESPN didn't let fans hear what was said. The network failed to play the audio from Teague, who was mic'd up.

According to Little League observers on Facebook, coaches "receive a blanket warning" at the start of tournaments that there is a zero tolerance policy on arguing with umpires. Add in the fact that coaches are mic'd up and it's extremely rare for a Little League coach to be ejected from the World Series or regional tournaments.

In the Little League rule book, Rule 9.02(b) states: If a manager believes a decision conflicts with the written rules (a misapplication of a rule, not a judgment call), the manager may request "Time." Once the home plate umpire grants time, the manager (and only the head manager) may approach the umpire who made the call to politely ask for clarification or appeal.

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST SPORTS NEWS

Based on the ejection, the umpire seems to have applied this exact rule to give Teague the boot. How did fans react online? About as you'd expect. It was a mixed bag of people arguing it was soft to kick the coach out of a meaningful game while others argued that Teague was foolish for thinking he could push the envelope.

STAY "FEARLESS" ON THE GO! TAKE TOMI LAHREN WITH YOU. DOWNLOAD THE TLIF PODCAST NOW!

"They were down 6-0 was tossing him even worth it? No. Umpire try to show off....nothing more," one fan wrote on Facebook in support of Teague.

Meanwhile, on the opposite side, a fan took a shot at the coach and his shorts, writing, "Balls & Strikes arguments = zero and non-starter. Already warned- he can take his Ralph Lauren shorts to the BUS."

You get the idea. Emotions are high this time of year. We're talking about 12-year-old baseball, TV, glory and fame. Add it up and you have a powder keg of emotions just waiting to boil over.

item.title: Cruz sounds alarm over $400M Hamas-era provision in Board of Peace plan — issues blunt warning
item.description: Sen. Ted Cruz says he's deeply concerned about a Board of Peace provision that could cover up to $400 million in debts from Hamas' rule in Gaza.
item.content:encoded:
U.S. officials have for years warned that Hamas has exploited ostensibly civilian and humanitarian funding streams to support its terrorist infrastructure, fueling concerns over whether money entering Gaza can be kept out of the terror group's hands as a new U.S.-backed governing structure prepares to take control.

The Treasury Department has repeatedly targeted what it describes as Hamas financing networks, including a secret investment portfolio, sham charities and organizations that raised money under the guise of humanitarian work while supporting Hamas' military wing.

Those concerns resurfaced this week after Israel's Kan News reported that a provision in the Board of Peace's Gaza roadmap could allow up to $400 million to address unpaid obligations accumulated during Hamas' rule, including money owed to public-sector workers, suppliers and contractors.

The dispute is over whether a successor government can settle legitimate obligations inherited from nearly two decades of Hamas rule without indirectly benefiting the terrorist group. Critics warn that doing so could relieve financial burdens associated with Hamas' rule or create opportunities for the group to siphon off resources while it retains influence on the ground. Board officials argue the mechanism is instead designed to allow a successor government to preserve essential services and relationships with legitimate workers and suppliers — with each claim individually vetted and any payment that could benefit Hamas rejected.

TRUMP ADMINISTRATION PROBES UNRWA OVER ALLEGED EMPLOYMENT OF 1,500 TERRORISTS

Nickolay Mladenov, the Board of Peace's high representative for Gaza, sharply rejected the characterization that the provision amounted to a financial agreement with Hamas.

"The claims that there is a financial agreement between the Board of Peace and Hamas are false," Mladenov wrote in Hebrew on X Wednesday, adding that no such proposal had been "discussed, negotiated, or considered." He said the Board's objective remained the complete disarmament of Hamas and the establishment of civilian governance backed by an international security presence.

Sen. Ted Cruz, R-Texas, told Fox News Digital that he remained alarmed by the provision.

"I'm deeply concerned about these reports. Terrorists use money as fungible and they build credibility by having international donors finance their debts, which is why Congress long ago banned money from going to Palestinian governments in the West Bank," Cruz said.

"We also know that international donors paid for Hamas to build terrorist infrastructure across the Gaza Strip in the first place, and shouldn't be trusted to direct reimbursement money," Cruz continued. "Hamas should be utterly eradicated before new resources flow into Gaza."

HAMAS AGREES TO COMPLETE DISARMAMENT UNDER 'HISTORIC' GAZA AGREEMENT: TRUMP

A senior Board of Peace official, speaking to Fox News Digital on background Thursday, pushed back on the premise that the roadmap commits $400 million to paying Hamas' debts.

"There's really just a commitment to analyze when we get the data. There's no commitment to fund anything. We don't have an obligation to even do $400 million," the official said.

The official described the provision as a three-year review process, capped at $400 million, under which the successor Gaza administration could determine whether particular unpaid obligations need to be resolved in order to maintain essential services and relationships with legitimate suppliers.

HILLARY CLINTON BREAKS WITH DEMOCRATIC CRITICS BY BACKING TRUMP’S GAZA PLAN AS THE 'ONLY GAME IN TOWN'

"This notion that there's, like, a $400 million payoff vehicle, Hamas kind of has a commitment for it — none of that is true," the official said. "If anybody's gonna start running with a narrative that a $400 million committed tab is beginning now ... that would just be incorrect reporting. That's not the deal."

"No one's picking up a tab right now," the official added, saying any review would take place only after the new Gaza administration gains access to financial records allowing it to determine who the creditors are, what services they provided and whether those relationships are needed going forward.

"Even the first dollar of the $400 million, we're going to evaluate that first dollar," the official said. "It's not going to be a blank check handed to Hamas. It's going to be evaluated, rigorously analyzed."

The official compared the process to a corporate restructuring, arguing that while Hamas is being permanently removed from government, the successor administration cannot necessarily walk away from every legitimate obligation accumulated during the previous government's rule.

HAMAS SAYS IT WILL DISSOLVE GAZA GOVERNMENT, BUT ISRAEL WARNS GROUP STILL SEEKS HEZBOLLAH-STYLE CONTROL

He offered the example of a European pharmaceutical company that supplied medicine to Gaza hospitals but was never paid. If the new administration needs that company to continue supplying medicine, he said, resolving some of its unpaid invoices could be necessary to maintain the relationship.

"The theme here, really, is continuity of services," the official said.

The official did not say that Hamas would have to be fully disarmed across the entire Gaza Strip before the first claim could potentially be paid.

"The reality is that this is going to be community by community," the official said, explaining that the successor administration is expected to move into individual areas as Hamas disarms there.

IRAN REAFFIRMS SUPPORT FOR HAMAS AS TRUMP PUSHES TO DISARM TERROR GROUP

Asked whether Hamas would have to be completely removed from Gaza before the new administration could resolve an outstanding liability — for example, involving a hospital in Rafah — the official said a payment could occur even if Hamas had not yet been fully removed elsewhere in the Strip.

"The idea is that where those decisions are made, Hamas is not gonna be there," he said.

When Fox News Digital asked specifically whether it was accurate to say money would not be transferred into areas where Hamas remained in control, the official said: "It's accurate to say."

The official acknowledged that more complicated cases could arise if the same supplier operates in both Hamas-free and Hamas-controlled portions of Gaza. Officials might then have to determine whether to reimburse only the portion associated with the area controlled by the successor government or negotiate some other arrangement necessary to maintain the service.

US URGES DONORS TO ABANDON UNRWA FUNDING AS UN DEFENDS AGENCY'S MISSION

Cruz's central criticism is that money is fungible: if international donors satisfy obligations accumulated under Hamas rule, resources that might otherwise have been needed to cover those liabilities could theoretically be used elsewhere.

The Board official rejected that argument, saying Hamas is insolvent and was never going to pay many of the outstanding creditors in the first place.

"It's not as though we're alleviating them from, like, their budget that they actually were gonna actually go pay that $100 and now they get to save it," the official said.

"They were never paying it in the first place," he continued. "We're making a decision separate and apart from Hamas, whether this fits into our budget and our relationships."

HAMAS TAPS 'ULTIMATE INSTITUTIONAL SURVIVOR' AS TERROR CHIEF, SENDING MESSAGE TO ISRAEL: EXPERT

The official described Hamas as "dead insolvent right now" and "financially, completely, completely in shambles."

Fox News Digital also pressed the official on a separate concern: even if money is never transferred directly to Hamas, could the group extract taxes, payments or other benefits from suppliers or employees receiving funds while it remains armed elsewhere?

"If there's a risk that some of the money is going to still end up in the hands of Hamas, then we're gonna shut it down," the official said.

He said officials would examine each recipient, the services provided and where the money ultimately would go.

"If Hamas is not fully disarmed ... can it end up in their hands? If the answer to that question is yes, then they're not gonna get money," he said. "Like, that is crystal clear."

The official also disclosed that the Board intends to try to recover assets it believes Hamas stole and use those assets, where possible, to satisfy legitimate obligations.

"We are going to make a real effort to go and try to recover those assets and use some of those assets, where we have found theft ... to satisfy some of these obligations," he said.

If recovered assets are insufficient, the official said outside funding would come from countries in the region rather than Washington.

"This is coming from regional partners. This is not coming from the United States," he said.

item.title: Luigi Mangione expected to plead guilty in federal case: reports
item.description: Luigi Mangione is expected to plead guilty to federal stalking charges in the UnitedHealthcare CEO case, potentially delaying his New York City trial.
item.content:encoded:
Accused UnitedHealthcare CEO assassin Luigi Mangione is expected to plead guilty to the federal charges against him at a surprise pretrial conference Friday, according to local reports, a move that could upend his state-level murder trial just weeks before it's supposed to begin in New York City.

State and federal prosecutors and Mangione's legal team have not responded to requests for comment from Fox News Digital.

But two of the city's major newspapers, the New York Post and New York Times, both reported Thursday that the 28-year-old former Ivy Leaguer is expected to plead guilty in his federal stalking case.

LUIGI MANGIONE HEARING SET FOR FRIDAY STIRS PLEA DEAL SPECULATION IN HIS FEDERAL CASE

Mangione is accused of following UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson to a Manhattan Hilton hotel on the morning of Dec. 4, 2024, and shooting him in the back hours before a business conference was supposed to take place there. Surveillance video shows a man in a hoodie approach Thompson from behind and open fire with a handgun — the same weapon authorities allege Mangione had in his backpack when he was arrested in a Pennsylvania McDonald's five days later.

Mangione has pleaded not guilty to all charges in both cases previously. His defense team has had some success already, convincing judges in both cases to dismiss the most serious charges. As a result, he would no longer face capital punishment if convicted in a federal trial, and would not face life without parole if convicted in New York state.

FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE

He could still face a maximum sentence of life without parole in federal prison if convicted in that case — but experts say he would probably avoid the stiffest possible sentence even if convicted by a jury.

LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

"Rarely somebody with no background, who’s educated, gets the maximum sentences," said Donna Rotunno, a Chicago criminal defense attorney and Fox News contributor. "Is he looking at minimum sentences? No. But at the end of the day, he’s benefiting from more serious charges being dismissed."

He is still likely looking at decades behind bars, and any legal issues arising from a potential plea deal could also delay the start of his state trial, which is supposed to begin with jury selection on Sept. 8, she said.

item.title: 10 House incumbent lawmakers who saw their 2026 re-election bids end in primary defeat
item.description: 10 incumbent U.S. House lawmakers so far have lost their primaries while running in the 2026 election cycle, including three Republicans and seven Democrats.
item.content:encoded:
So far during the 2026 election season, 10 incumbent House lawmakers have lost primaries, including three Republicans and seven Democrats.

The three Republican incumbents who fell short include Dan Crenshaw of Texas, Thomas Massie of Kentucky, and Andy Ogles of Tennessee.

The seven incumbent House Democrats who lost include Al Green of Texas, Julie Johnson of Texas, Dan Goldman of New York, Adriano Espaillat of New York, Diana DeGette of Colorado, Shri Thanedar of Michigan, and John Larson of Connecticut.

The failed Texas and Tennessee U.S. House incumbents grappled with redistricting in their states that applied to this cycle.

Crenshaw, the only U.S. House Republican incumbent seeking re-election in Texas who did not get President Donald Trump's endorsement, lost the GOP primary for Texas' 2nd Congressional District to state Rep. Steve Toth.

While Trump did not endorse either of the men ahead of the primary, he has since endorsed Toth.

Crenshaw has served in the House since 2019.

MTG SAYS GOP'S FUTURE 'DESTROYED' AFTER TRUMP-BACKED PRIMARY CHALLENGER DEFEATS THOMAS MASSIE

Massie lost the Republican primary for Kentucky's 4th Congressional District to Trump-backed challenger Ed Gallrein, a former Navy SEAL.

The race made history as the most expensive U.S. House primary contest ever, reports indicate.

Massie has served in the U.S. House of Representatives since late 2012.

Despite having Trump's endorsement, Ogles lost the GOP primary for Tennessee's 5th Congressional District to former state Agriculture Commissioner Charlie Hatcher.

Ogles has served in the House since 2023.

Trump backed Hatcher last week after he defeated Ogles in the primary.

"Last night was another good night for Endorsements, 8-1, and the 1 was a person who I remained loyal to even though he had virtually no chance of winning, and was running against a Great 'Trump' Candidate, and former Agricultural Commissioner of Tennessee, named Charlie Hatcher. Good luck Charlie! Run tough and hard. You have my Complete and Total Endorsement!" Trump declared in a Truth Social post.

DSA-BACKED CANDIDATE TOPPLES MILLIONAIRE DEM INCUMBENT

Thanedar, who has served as a lawmaker in the lower congressional chamber since 2023, lost the Democratic U.S. House primary in Michigan's 13th Congressional District this year to state Rep. Donavan McKinney, a Democratic socialist.

Thanedar declared in October 2023 that he was renouncing Democratic Socialists of America membership, though then-Detroit DSA co-chair Mikal Goodman declared at the time in a post on X that Thanedar "was expelled as a member on September 17th, by 91% of vote the general membership. He no longer had a membership to renounce."

item.title: Matthew McConaughey prompts priceless reaction from Ella Langley after Oscar winner covers ‘Choosin’ Texas’
item.description: Matthew McConaughey grabbed a mandolin to perform a bluegrass cover of Ella Langley's "Choosin' Texas" on "The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon."
item.content:encoded:
Matthew McConaughey is a Texas boy at heart.

During Wednesday's episode of "The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon," the 56-year-old actor embraced his Southern roots by performing Ella Langley's hit song, "Choosin' Texas," alongside Fallon and indie folk band The Last Bison. The cover quickly drew attention on social media and even earned a response from Langley herself.

"I don't think I'll ever recover from this," Langley wrote on her Instagram Stories alongside a video of McConaughey and Fallon jamming to her hit song.

KOE WETZEL AND ELLA LANGLEY RELEASE NEW COUNTRY SONG 'JADED' AND IT'S ALREADY GOING VIRAL

Fans shared a similar sentiment.

"POV me driving singing this with my whole chest," one fan commented.

"The cover we didn’t know we needed," another wrote.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

The performance unfolded during a new installment of "Tonight Show Audience Suggestion Box," when Fallon read a submission that combined Langley’s hit with McConaughey’s latest movie, "The Rivals of Amziah King."

"I love that song ‘Choosin’ Texas’ by Ella Langley," Fallon read. "And I’m really excited to see Matthew McConaughey’s new movie ‘The Rivals of Amziah King,’ where he performs in a bluegrass band. If there was only a way to combine those things, that would be a dream come true."

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"This is ‘The Tonight Show,’ where dreams become reality," Fallon quipped.

Moments later, the curtain opened to reveal McConaughey with a mandolin in hand alongside The Last Bison, while Fallon joined in on the washboard. The group then launched into a bluegrass rendition of Langley's chart-topping hit.

McConaughey's cover comes as "Choosin' Texas" continues to make history for Langley.

ELLA LANGLEY'S 'CHOOSIN' TEXAS' SPENDS 15 WEEKS AT NUMBER ONE ON THE BILLBOARD HOT 100

The country anthem recently scored its 17th nonconsecutive week at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100, making it the longest-running non-holiday No. 1 by a solo female artist in the chart's history.

The milestone pushed Langley past Whitney Houston's "I Will Always Love You" and Mariah Carey's "We Belong Together," which each spent 14 weeks at the top of the chart.

For McConaughey, the song choice was particularly fitting.

The Oscar-winning actor has long been outspoken about his love for the Lone Star State, where he was born and later returned to raise his family.

‘SOPRANOS’ STAR JAMIE-LYNN SIGLER FLED HOLLYWOOD FOR TEXAS WHERE SHE NO LONGER FEELS ‘WATCHED’

McConaughey left Malibu, California, for Austin, Texas, with his wife, Camila Alves McConaughey, and their three children in 2014. He previously explained that returning to Texas was always part of his plan once he started a family.

"This has always been home, there are multiple reasons for that," McConaughey previously said during an appearance on "Today."

The "Dallas Buyers Club" star said his mother and two older brothers were also in Texas and explained that he wanted his children to experience some of the same values he grew up around.

"I wanted them to have what I grew up around," he said, adding that there is a certain amount of "common sense" that comes with life in Texas.

item.title: Bride serves McDonald's customer in wedding dress while tying knot at restaurant: 'Handing out extra sauces'
item.description: An Ohio McDonald's hosted the viral wedding of co-workers Jamie and George Callicoat, who spoke to Fox News Digital about the unusual venue they chose.
item.content:encoded:
A Northeast Ohio McDonald's restaurant was transformed into a wedding venue last Saturday as two co-workers said "I do" in front of friends, family, fellow employees and the occasional customer.

"We had people trying to come in the lobby the whole time," despite the dining room being closed to the public for the ceremony and reception, bride Jamie Callicoat, of Akron, Ohio, told Fox News Digital this week after marrying co-worker George Callicoat.

"I was handing out extra sauces to an actual customer in my wedding dress."

'MCDONALD'S CHANGED THE COURSE OF MY LIFE': CONGRESSMAN SELLS BUSINESS HE BUILT SINCE HIS TEEN YEARS

Some customers made it to the kiosks inside to order, and the drive-thru remained open throughout the celebration. Everyone — including unsuspecting customers — "rolled with the punches," Jamie said.

"It's still work, if you're there off the clock, on the clock, whatever," she said. "We were there interrupting to have our personal wedding."

The intimate ceremony has since gone viral online.

"Social media content surrounding the wedding has already generated more than 20 million impressions across Instagram and Facebook, with the story continuing to spread," McDonald's of Northeast Ohio said in a news release.

MCDONALD'S NEWEST MENU ITEM HAS FANS BEGGING FOR ONE DISCONTINUED FAVORITE

"We kind of figured it would get some attention, but this is just unreal," Jamie said of the reaction.

The newlyweds were back at work on the Tuesday after their wedding as customers and others who frequent the restaurant began congratulating them.

"Our Brinks guys, who come and pick up our money, came in and they both walked right up to us and said, 'Oh my gosh, we've seen the video. Congratulations!'" Jamie said.

"It's wild. It's really fun, though."

Jamie is a manager at the McDonald's where she wed George, the restaurant's crew trainer.

The pair met through mutual friends at Cedar Point in Ohio in June 2025 and went on a few dates. When Jamie moved to Akron and began working at the McDonald's in October 2025, George trained her.

Jamie said George's personality drew her to him.

"We just get along very well," she said. "I love everything about George. He's a great guy."

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"I love everything about her," George told Fox News Digital. "She is a wonderful person, very caring, very kind."

The pair became engaged at Cedar Point and initially planned to get married there, too. Then a district manager jokingly suggested they tie the knot at the McDonald's where they both work.

"We thought about it for a day or so and went back and were like, 'Well, were you guys serious?'" Jamie recalled. "And one thing kind of led to another, and here we are."

The celebration became a team effort, McDonald's said in its news release.

"Crew members and managers came together to help make the couple's wedding day special, providing dinner, a wedding cake and other touches for the celebration," McDonald's said. "Even the officiant had a McDonald's connection: the husband of the restaurant's general manager performed the ceremony."

McDonald's provided the venue, and despite ultimately holding a larger celebration than the destination-style wedding they had originally envisioned, Jamie said the ceremony was "cost-effective."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

The couple handled some of the decorations and food themselves. Guests were served pulled barbecue chicken, buffalo chicken dip, homemade rigatoni and fried chicken, while the kids ate fresh McDonald's food.

Even the flower girl got a McDonald's touch, tossing petals from a Happy Meal box.

"That was my decision, mostly," Jamie said. "I mean, we work at McDonald's. I thought it was cute."

The official Instagram account for McDonald's commented on a video of the ceremony, writing, "A modern day love story."

"Congrats to them on their McMarriage!" wrote another well-wisher. "'Forever After All' and we're McLovin' it."

One commenter even joked about McDonald's notoriously finicky soft-serve machines, but George said theirs wasn't a problem.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

"Ours is always working, unless it's being cleaned," he said.

Tammy Snider, the location's general manager, said it was "so much more than a wedding at a McDonald's."

"It's a story about two people in love and a restaurant team that wanted to make sure they felt celebrated," Snider said. "Our restaurants are places where friendships are made, milestones are celebrated and communities come together. George and Jamie's wedding is such a beautiful example of that."

Jamie called it a "perfect" outcome.

"We had a great time," she said. "Our co-workers are amazing, our bosses are amazing and McDonald's is amazing for allowing us to do this."

item.title: Jack Story skipped his high school graduation to go bass fishing and walked away with $100K
item.description: Jack Story skipped his high school graduation to compete in the Bass Fishing League All-American on Lake Murray and he won $100,000 at age 18.
item.content:encoded:
Jack Story didn’t walk across the stage at his high school graduation. He was too busy winning $100,000.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

The 18-year-old Georgia angler made the decision earlier this year to skip his graduation ceremony and compete in the Phoenix Bass Fishing League All-American on Lake Murray. Looking back now, it doesn’t sound like he lost much sleep over it.

During a recent interview with OutKick Outdoors, Story said he originally qualified through a regional tournament and "never really expected" to make it to the All-American. But once he found out the tournament landed on the same day as graduation, the choice was pretty simple.

"I was going fishing, and they could either be accommodating or not," Story said. "Thankfully, they were very helpful with it."

His school wasn’t completely thrilled, though. Story said the headmaster and others at the school "handled it about as well as they could have," even if they would have preferred to see him in a cap and gown.

Still, some tried to make him reconsider.

"One of my teachers kind of hinted that I should be at graduation," Story said. "But it just wasn’t even an option."

Watch Jack Story's full interview with OutKick Outdoors here:

Story went on to win the All-American and the $100,000 prize that came with it. He also qualified for REDCREST 2027 and the Toyota Series Championship — a pretty strong consolation prize for missing a graduation ceremony.

Still, even weeks later, he said the whole thing feels surreal.

"It was so stressful during the tournament that I think it was a huge relief, but I also didn’t even know what to do," Story said. "The feeling of accomplishment doesn’t even register. Looking back on it, it doesn’t feel real."

The win also came with a little family bragging rights.

Story’s dad previously fished the All-American and finished 34th. So yes, beating him was somewhere on the checklist.

"I thought that was going to be pretty easy given the lake it was on," Story said.

But that wasn’t the only goal. Story said he wanted to beat the other two anglers from his regional and keep advancing. Instead, he ended up winning the whole thing.

His dad’s advice has always been simple: If you’re going to do something, go all in. That applied to fishing, too.

"If I wanted to skip school to go fish, I was at least going to actually fish," Story said. "His thing was, if you’re going to fish, you’re going to fish all day. Just dedicate yourself to it."

That mindset mattered at Lake Murray. Because Story’s victory was anything but smooth.

The final day came down to 10 ounces, and Story said he knew it was going to be close. What made it worse was the fact that he had already been hit with penalties after issues with his livewells and oxygen tank.

"I was really stressed out about the fact that I could lose because of penalties," Story said. "I’d rather lose by 10 pounds than lose by any sort of penalty."

In other words, this was not some easy stroll to a giant check.

"No, very far from," Story said.

DENNY HAMLIN CHASES MONSTER LARGEMOUTH BASS IN TEXAS WITH BASSMASTER PRO CHRIS ZALDAIN

There was also the added pressure of chasing history. Now the tournament's youngest winner ever, Story broke a 15-year record previously held by Jacob Wheeler — one of the biggest names in the sport.

Unfortunately, Story found out about the record before the tournament was over.

"I honestly wish I would have figured that out after, rather than the night of day two," Story said. "Somebody texted me, and I was like, ‘Dude, that is not what I needed.’ It made it more stressful because instantly, that became my goal."

Since the win, Story said life has included more interviews, podcasts and attention. But mostly, it has included more fishing.

He had a rough finish in a high school tournament shortly after the All-American, and that did not sit well with him.

"I hate losing in fishing, especially when it’s to one of my friends," Story said. "I’ve got to get my get-back, if that makes sense. I want to go beat them again the next day. I just want to fish, and I want to win."

Story is headed to Carson-Newman, where he plans to fish in college. He is also considering fishing the Tackle Warehouse Invitationals if he can make the schedule work.

"Might as well," he said.

For other kids who want to get into competitive fishing, Story said persistence matters. So does helping parents understand that fishing can create real opportunities, including scholarships.

"I don’t think people really realize that you can get a scholarship for fishing," Story said. "If you dedicate yourself and put in the constructive work to get there, I think it’s easier than people make it seem. You just have to know how to do it."

More than that, Story said fishing gave him something positive to pour himself into.

"I’m out of trouble because I fish," he said. "It keeps you out of trouble. You’re doing something outdoors. It’s good."

And even after winning $100,000 at 18 years old, Story is already thinking about helping more kids get on the water.

"I really enjoy taking the younger generation fishing," Story said. "I think every kid deserves the opportunity to fish, and that’s that."

They were discussing a new bill in Pennsylvania that would change pets from being considered property to members of the family in a divorce, according to People.

The couple rescued Lena, a Maltese and Shih Tzu mix, in 2021 after she was featured in a pet adoption segment on the show.

item.title: Justice Department slams 'politically motivated demands' of DC Council asking govs to remove National Guard
item.description: The Justice Department slammed D.C. Council letters urging governors to recall National Guard troops, calling the demands "impotent theatrics."
item.content:encoded:
The Justice Department slammed the D.C. Council for its "politically motivated demands" and "impotent theatrics" after its members sent letters to governors asking them to recall their National Guard troops from the nation’s capital.

The development comes as FBI Director Kash Patel told Fox News Digital this week that "homicides in D.C. are down an incredible 44% from last year" when President Donald Trump’s administration launched the Safe and Beautiful initiative in Washington, D.C., which increased the federal law enforcement presence and deployed hundreds of federal agents and National Guard troops to combat crime.

"I am not surprised that your recent letter to state governors regarding the National Guard feigns ignorance of the historic public safety strides made in our Nation's capital since August 11, 2025," Assistant Attorney General Colin McDonald wrote in a letter addressed to the D.C. Council. "I am surprised and saddened, however, that you would show such callousness — instead of compassion and care — toward your constituents, who now live in a city with far less violence and fear thanks to the National Guard and the D.C. Safe and Beautiful Task Force."

"Let me be clear, your council has no power to demand that governors remove their brave men and women from serving in uniform in our Nation's capital. Your politically-motivated letter is impotent theatrics not worth the paper it's written on, and D.C. is a much safer place no matter what you say," McDonald added. "Because you refuse to speak the truth about the life-preserving work of the Task Force, the truth will speak for itself."

FBI TOUTS 6,000 ARRESTS, 44% HOMICIDE DROP ONE YEAR INTO TRUMP'S DC CRIME CRACKDOWN

The Justice Department said in a message on X that "This Department of Justice will not stand for these politically motivated demands."

"We will continue standing with @POTUS and the Make D.C. Safe and Beautiful Task Force to deliver historic results for the community — and for visitors from across the country and around the world to enjoy," it added.

Fox News Digital has reached out to representatives of D.C. Council members for comment.

The letters, co-signed by the D.C. Council members, were sent to the governors of Alabama, Alaska, Arkansas, Florida, Georgia, Hawaii, Idaho, Indiana, Louisiana, Mississippi, Montana, Nebraska, Nevada, North Carolina, Oklahoma, Puerto Rico, South Carolina, Tennessee, West Virginia and Wyoming in late July, according to the office of Councilmember At-Large Robert White.

Each letter opened the same, saying, "We write as elected officials representing the District of Columbia to respectfully request that you withdraw all troops currently deployed to the District by September 1, 2026."

DC MURDER RATE SEES ASTONISHING TURNAROUND AS TRUMP TEAM CREDITS FEDERAL CRACKDOWN

"There are approximately 5,148 Guard personnel currently deployed to the District under the premise that an extraordinary military presence was necessary to address public safety. Yet analysis of the deployment has found only a modest decrease in property crime and no measurable reduction in violent crime attributable to the Guard’s presence since August 2025," the letters continue.

"The deployment has, however, cost American taxpayers more than $3 million per day, according to the nonpartisan Congressional Budget Office. Continuing this deployment despite the absence of a demonstrated violent-crime benefit would misuse both taxpayer dollars — in the billions, if maintained for years at its expanded scale — and the service of the Guard member themselves," the letters add, claiming that at a time where families in each of the states "and across the country are struggling with the cost of groceries, housing, health care, and other necessities, wasting those resources on an ineffective, indefinite deployment that neither District residents nor officials asked for is disrespectful to American taxpayers."

The letters conclude by saying that: "We recognize that the America 250 events present significant public safety and logistical challenges for the District and have required coordination across multiple jurisdictions. We are grateful to the Guard members who have been present to support the nation’s capital during this exceptionally busy period. Once the principal event-related needs conclude on September 1, 2026, we respectfully ask that they be permitted to return home to their families, careers and communities, rather than remain indefinitely assigned to a costly mission that has not demonstrated a measurable impact on violent crime."

However, McDonald said in his letter "Thanks to courageous and steadfast support from National Guard units, Task Force members have conducted thousands of arrests, located lost and missing children, and taken substantial numbers of illegal firearms off the city's streets" and that the National Guard "has personally intervened in numerous assaults and provided medical aid on innumerable occasions, including repeatedly administering life-saving NARCAN to citizens in peril."

"While you slander these men and women as ‘outside military forces,’ I refer to them as true American heroes," he also said. "You should withdraw your letters and dedicate your remaining time in public service to correcting D.C.'s laws to ensure criminals are punished and the public is protected — not the other way around."

Fox News Digital’s Michael Sinkewicz contributed to this report.

item.title: Trump admin marks 15 straight months with zero border releases as apprehensions plunge 94%

President Donald Trump's administration says it has gone 15 straight months without a single release at the border as of Thursday.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin's office says daily apprehensions at the border are down 94% compared to former President Joe Biden's administration and are at the lowest level seen in 30 years.

"Again this month, the results are clear: President Trump’s border security agenda is restoring order and putting the safety of the American people first," Mullin said in a statement.

"DHS remains focused on enforcing our immigration laws, securing the border, and ensuring those who enter our country illegally are removed swiftly. Thanks to the strong leadership of President Trump, we have the most secure border in history," he added.

'AMERICA FIRST' IMMIGRATION OVERHAUL BILL WOULD CODIFY TRUMP'S CAMPAIGN PROMISES ONCE AND FOR ALL

Meanwhile, seizures of contraband at the border in July were 26% higher than under Biden, with authorities seizing cocaine, methamphetamine, heroin, fentanyl and marijuana.

INSIDE UNDERGROUND EL PASO STORM DRAIN SYSTEM BORDER PATROL SAYS CARTELS EXPLOIT TO SMUGGLE ILLEGAL MIGRANTS

U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) also helped enforce Trump's tariff policies, flagging $23 billion in duties identified for collection in July alone.

"Clear policy, strong enforcement, and dedicated frontline personnel are delivering results at our borders," CBP Commissioner Rodney Scott said in a statement.

"With the support of President Trump and Secretary Mullin, CBP is securing our nation against illegal crossings, dangerous individuals, and illicit drugs while keeping lawful trade and travel moving. These results show what is possible when border security is treated as a national priority," he added.

The Trump administration is still moving to increase its immigration enforcement efforts. Last month, the House of Representatives moved toward codifying several of Trump's immigration orders.

The Permanent Trump Secure Border Act would criminalize visa overstays and increase penalties for unlawful entry, would effectively end "catch and release" policies by requiring most illegal migrants to be detained or returned while their cases are pending and tighten asylum eligibility and humanitarian parole, among other provisions.

The measure would also bolster the CBP by directing the DHS to modernize border facilities, expand staffing and workforce planning and deploy more surveillance technology, including drones, radar systems, biometric screening and DNA collection.

Fox News' Adam Pack contributed to this report.

item.title: Warren’s ancestry saga roars back after Dem ally touts Native Senate first: ‘Arrows fired’
item.description: Elizabeth Warren's past Native American claims face a new criticisms as Minnesota's Democratic Senate nominee says no Native woman has served in the US Senate.
item.content:encoded:
Minnesota Democratic Senate nominee Peggy Flanagan is pitching donors on the prospect of becoming the first Native American woman to serve in the U.S. Senate — drawing attention to one of her prominent endorsers, Sen. Elizabeth Warren, whose past claims of Native American identity became a yearslong political controversy.

"In almost 250 years, there’s never been a Native woman serving in the US Senate. It’s time to change that," the email reads. "I am Ojibwe and a proud member of the White Earth Nation. My family is the Wolf Clan. The mission of my clan is to never leave anyone behind — and that’s been my guiding principle … Right now, there are no Native voices in the US Senate. If I win this race, we can change that."

Throughout her career, Warren identified herself as a Native American, writing "American Indian" on her Texas bar-registration card and describing herself as a minority in the Association of American Law Schools directory. Since 2019, Warren has walked back her indigenous identity, clarifying that she is not a person of color nor a citizen of a tribe, and stating that she should not have identified herself as an American Indian.

TAFOYA MAKES 'COMMON SENSE' PITCH TO DISAFFECTED DEMOCRATS AS SHE VOWS TO FIGHT MINNESOTA’S ‘SOCIALIST LURCH’

Warren supported Flanagan in Minnesota's Democratic Senate primary.

"The Democrat nominee for Senate in Minnesota, Peggy Flanagan , just sent out a fundraising email on the DNC list that admits that Elizabeth Warren is NOT Native American," conservative commentator Steve Guest posted to X, adding, "tough break for Fauxcahontas."

"Has anybody checked on Elizabeth Warren?" the Republican Party quipped on X.

"Elizabeth Warren just took her peace pipe and went home to throw a tantrum," another user replied.

WARREN PUSHED ‘FREE AND EASY’ IRS FILING SYSTEM, BUT DOCS REVEAL WHAT SHE USED INSTEAD

President Donald Trump famously lampooned Warren’s claimed ancestry by labeling her "Pocahontas." The feud between the two culminated in Warren taking a genetic test in 2018, which found she was between 0.1% and 1.6% Native American.

"Excuse me? How dare she disrespect Elizabeth Warren like that?" libertarian commentator Brad Polumbo wrote, ironically.

ELIZABETH WARREN CONFRONTED ON CALLING CONTROVERSIAL SENATE CANDIDATE GRAHAM PLATNER HER 'KIND OF MAN'

Multiple X users posted AI-generated images of Warren in Native American garb looking dejected or angry in response to the fundraising email.

"Elizabeth Warren is doing a land acknowledgement on Flanagan's head," New York Post columnist Kirsten Fleming quipped.

"I can say this because I am part of the Cherokee Nation, but these two should powwow over this," podcaster Dave Van de Walle joked.

The Flanagan campaign and Warren’s office did not respond to requests for comment when reached by Fox News Digital on Thursday.
